summary: Planet SPHEREx-X is a free website that turns NASA SPHEREx images of the sky into short videos. Search for a star or enter sky coordinates, and it collects all images of that area and plays them together so you can see objects move or change. Click an object to view its infrared data and how its brightness changes over time. The tool also scans the sky to find moving objects, changes in brightness, and possible brown dwarfs. It can track asteroids and comets, find ice and methane, and estimate the distance to nearby brown dwarfs. New NASA data appears automatically, so anyone can explore the sky and help discover new objects.
details:
What it does

Planet SPHEREx-X lets anyone explore how the sky changes over time using NASA SPHEREx images. You can search for a star or location and watch all available images as a short movie. Moving objects appear to jump, while objects that change brightness flicker.

You can also:

  • Choose colours: Explore all 102 infrared colours or focus on water ice, methane and other gases.
  • Compare images: Combine pictures, highlight moving objects, or show areas that changed.
  • Study objects: Click any object to see its infrared data and brightness over time. You can also download the data.
  • Add star maps: Show known stars, asteroids and comets to help identify objects.
  • Share views: Copy a link that saves all your current settings.

Other features

  • Automatic search: Finds moving objects, changing stars, possible brown dwarfs and objects only visible in infrared.
  • Identify objects: Compares their light patterns with known stars and brown dwarfs to estimate their type, temperature and distance.
  • Measure distance: Uses changes in an object's position as Earth moves around the Sun to estimate how far away it is.
  • Track moving objects: Follows asteroids and comets while keeping them in the centre of the images.
  • Map ice and gases: Shows where water ice, methane, CO₂ and CO appear in the sky.
  • Save and explore: Save discoveries, download reports, view objects in other astronomy tools and watch for new data.

How it works

  • Backend: Uses Python to find and download small parts of NASA's image files instead of downloading entire files.
  • Frontend: Uses React and TypeScript to display images and handle colours, brightness and comparisons.
  • Speed: Images begin loading within seconds, and full results usually take 15–45 seconds.
  • API: Provides a public API so other projects can use its data.

Why it matters

NASA collects far more sky data than people can study by hand. Planet SPHEREx-X makes this data easier for everyone to explore. It helps people find interesting objects, study them and possibly discover things that would otherwise go unnoticed.

Other considerations

  • New data: Automatically picks up new SPHEREx data without needing code changes.
  • Limitations: Clearly shows where measurements may be less accurate, such as distance estimates for objects that are far away.
  • Shared resources: Uses caching and careful requests to avoid overloading NASA's services.
